material_scope_limits: Identities are common (query_slot,negative_slot), not unique edges/node pair annotations. Existing fixed pool may duplicate edges; graph annotation is outside this reader.

Union minus common is disagreement including ties, not guaranteed strict member rescue or query-level routeability. Absence of common errors cannot guarantee a single member correctly ranks all500 candidates.

The reader exports margins only for common errors. Full strict rescue masks among noncommon pooled errors are not exported; saved banks can support that narrower diagnostic later without new forwards if authorized.

Selected VALID states and potentially different selected cycles are retrospective. J4 changes encoder and predictor as well as sharing. Common burden is factual association, not causal erasure, method novelty, a heldout guarantee or training-gradient attribution.
mechanism_readout: Large common surviving count L identifies a common pairwise obstruction to serving; at leastLstrict outrankers gives RR<=1/(1+L), andL>=10 excludesHits10 without recalculating MRR.
E-common slots strictly corrected by J4 or S identify a correctable error of the shared bank at the same retained candidate identity, rather than an inherently universally unsolvable query.

For each query compare minimum member strict-wrong count to common count and pooled strict-wrong count, all already exported. If minimum remains much above common, different offending negatives require different members; low common overlap alone is insufficient for a query router.

For nonnegative normalized raw-logit aggregation in real arithmetic, a common strictly wrong slot cannot be rescued by any weights or choosing a member; saved FP32 pooling/ties are checked explicitly viaL.
resource_scope: CPU reader, twelve source-authenticated banks, no model/checkpoint/input split loads/forwards. Prior D2 CPU reader runtime completed39 bank diagnostics in10.55s/~425MB; this full margin export is larger and its actual resource cost is not measured. Fixed600s/8GiB plus1GiB stdout result is suggested; no automatic expansion.
